messages:
maria.k: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking out loud about cross-pool compaction fallbacks when host-side offload causes fragmentation spikes. Proposal: allow a lightweight cross-pool steal + async compaction path as an intermediate fallback before aggressive evict+prefetch.
aj: Can you sketch the invariants? i.e., what guarantees does steal+async break vs preserve?
devin_w: Main thing is tenant residency SLA. Steal shouldn't violate reserved capacity or tenant quotas. We can only steal from soft-resident pages, not pinned or reserved pages.
sasha: Also watch for hotspot redistribution: stealing can increase latency for the donor tenant if done synchronously. Async compaction helps but we need backpressure signals.
maria.k: Right. Goals: 1) avoid big synchronous prefetchs across PCIe. 2) keep donor impact bounded (bounded-bytes-per-second). 3) make compaction low-overhead and incremental.
ben_p: How do we decide donor candidates? LRU across pools maybe? Prefer cold segments with high fragmentation metric.
aj: We should define a fragmentation score per arena: free-run-length histogram + utilization skew. If score > threshold, mark as donor candidate.
sasha: Also add a hysteresis window. Don't flip donors on transient spikes.
maria.k: Implementation sketch: - mark pool as donor if frag_score > F and resident_util < U - allow up to X bytes to be stolen per epoch from donor - stolen pages get a soft-migrate tag; receiver can use them immediately but compaction is scheduled asynchronously to repair holes.
aj: What about KV-cache / kv-cache residency? We can't steal active KV pages or we'll regress inference latency.
devin_w: We tag pages with "hotness" TTL. Hot pages (recently accessed within T_hot) are not eligible. KV cache items have a higher hotness weight.
ben_p: Telemetry: emit donor_rate, steal_bytes, compaction_latency, donor_impact_sample. We need a dashboard to see regressions.
infra-bot: deploy-check: config keys referenced: `compact.enable_crosspool`, `compact.frag_threshold`, `compact.steal_rate_limit` — ensure feature flag gated.
maria.k: Edge cases: host-pinned staging and pinned CPU-backed tensors. Those should be excluded. Also avoid cross-node when NUMA penalties high.
sasha: Another tradeoff: we may increase peak GPU working set during compaction because receiver holds both old+new mappings until donor frees them. We should bound concurrent compaction tasks.
aj: Could use copy-on-write style: receiver pages are allocated in place if possible, or we move smaller slabs first (coalesced ranges) to limit overhead.
maria.k: We also need an API boundary: allocator should expose a small set of ops: claim_candidate(pool_id, bytes) -> opaque_token; commit_migration(token) or abort_migration(token). That keeps runtime and allocator decoupled.
devin_w: That token can carry backpressure hints and allow rollback if donor suddenly has demand.
ben_p: Perf test plan: synthetic fragmentation generator + mixed inference load, measure tail latency regressions with/without cross-pool steal under different steal_rate limits.
maria.k: Follow-ups: I'll draft a short RFC with state machine and telemetry signals. Action items: maria.k to write RFC, aj to design frag_score formula, sasha to spec guardrails for KV/pinned pages, ben_p to add dashboards, devin_w to prototype token API. Ping me if you want to pair on the prototype.
